overview: JSON Formatter CLI is a small command-line script that reads JSON from standard input or a file, validates it against strict JSON rules, and prints a consistently indented version. It is aimed at developers who want a lightweight formatter for debugging, automation, and review without adding package dependencies. Because it is distributed as a single script, it can be added to local workflows, CI checks, or editor tasks with minimal setup.
usecases: Piping an API response through the script to make nested JSON readable before debugging.
Validating a configuration file in a pre-commit hook or CI step before it reaches production.
Reformatting minified JSON copied from logs or another tool into stable, reviewable output.
howto: Download the script and place it somewhere on your PATH or in your project.
Run it with a file argument or pipe JSON into it, such as `json-formatter input.json` or `curl ... | json-formatter`.
Inspect the pretty-printed output or non-zero exit status to catch validation errors.

faq.q: Does it support JSON5, comments, or trailing commas?
faq.a: No, it validates strict JSON only and will reject non-standard syntax.

faq.q: Is it a standalone binary with no runtime required?
faq.a: No, it is a script, so you still need a compatible runtime installed even though it has no external dependencies.
